text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 billing is concentrated at every complexity tier, including low-complexity patients, but only three documented 99215 claims came back, too few to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern. The provider's 99215 share exceeds the all-provider share in every complexity band, and the gap is widest on patients with 0 or 1 conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include visits coded only for routine follow-up (Z09, e.g., C0121562, C0121982), UTI (N39.0, e.g., C0121651) or rash (R21, e.g., C0121802), which rarely support high-complexity MDM. Against that, the 3 documented 99215 claims (C0121603, C0121687, C0122674) all showed high MDM, but three charts cannot outweigh the billing pattern, and the documentation is too thin to judge. The 8 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence that notes may be templated or inflated. A reviewer should first request records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the Z09, N39.0 and R21 visits, and check those notes for cloned or templated language."}
